We do not create new smells.
We recover real ones.

Every ANIMA fragrance begins not in a brief but in a memory. The perfumer goes there. They interview the people who remember it. They consult botanical records, olfactory literature, archive testimonies spanning decades. The composition emerges from documentation, not imagination. The result is a smell specific to a real coordinate — a real moment — that you can look up, verify, and return to in your own memory. This is the only claim in the fragrance industry that requires genuine evidence to make. We make it because we have the evidence.

The river district before the expressway. Hinoki cypress, tatami dust, river-stone mineral, and the cold clarity of water that has run through granite. Documented with the assistance of three temple archivists and a pre-Shinkansen travel journal.

Bitter Ganache, Frozen Air

Vis-à-vis — Ambery Gourmand, Crisp Spice
Add to Bag Try It First — 2 ml Sample
Narrative Story

I know what they say about us — that we're cold, that we hide — but they don't understand the economics of solitude. The snow is falling outside my window in that slow, deliberate way it does when the city has finally agreed to shut up, and I am exactly where I want to be: indoors, in the armchair with the broken spring, a book cracked open on my knee, and a pen in my hand because I still write my diary longhand, because the scratch of ink on paper is the only sound I want competing with the music in my headphones. On the counter there's ganache left too long, dark and sharp and grown-up and entirely without apology, bitter cocoa on the tongue, and through the window frame comes a cold, clean bite of frozen air. The frost outside, the gold inside — that's the trade I make every winter. It is not loneliness. It is a controlled, intellectual cocoon, and I am warm in it.

一、苦甘纳许，冻气

外面在下雪。不是那种好看的雪，是伦敦十二月常见的那种，灰扑扑的，落在窗台上就化成一摊脏水。我坐在屋里，椅子扶手塌了一边，坐久了腰疼，但我懒得换。书摊在膝盖上，翻到一半，笔搁在手边，日记本上是今天的日期，还没写。耳机里的音乐放完了，我没切歌，就让它静着。

空气里有一股苦味。厨房台面上那块黑巧克力甘纳许，下午做的时候多放了可可，现在凉透了，表面结了一层薄壳。苦得很干净，不甜，不讨好谁。窗外有风从窗框的缝里钻进来，贴着地面走，脚踝先感觉到，一阵一阵的，像被什么轻轻咬了一下。

这种日子，我谁也不见。不是不喜欢人，是见人太费力。要说话，要接住对方的话，要在合适的时候笑。一个人待着，什么都不用接。冷在外面，暖在里面，一本书，一支笔，一天就这么过去了。

Steamed Lactones & December Frost

Pro tempore — Warm Milk, Comforting Musk
Add to Bag Try It First — 2 ml Sample
Narrative Story

I am ten years old again the second my hands wrap around the mug. It's the old ceramic one, the one with the chip on the rim that Mum refuses to throw away, and the milk inside is steamed to that precise temperature that feels like a hug from the inside out. I sink into the sofa — the soft, sagging one in the living room of my hometown house, the one that still bears the faint ring stain from a hundred Sunday dinners — and through the window the December frost is painting its slow, white lace across the glass. The smell is lactonic and warm, sweet milk and clean cotton and something else, something that only exists in this house, in this room, on this kind of afternoon. It is the smell of being kept, of being allowed to be small again, and nothing is asked of me here. The world outside is grey and hurried; in here, time moves at the speed of a snowflake. I take a sip, and I am home.

二、蒸奶内酯，十二月霜

杯子还是那只，杯口有一个小豁口，我妈说过好几次要扔，我没让。牛奶在锅里热到冒气，不能滚，滚了就老，倒进杯子里正好烫手心。我两只手捧着，从厨房走到客厅，坐下来，沙发陷下去一个坑，是我从小坐到大的那个位置。

老家的客厅不大，茶几上铺着一块勾花的白布，边角洗得发毛了。窗外在下霜，薄薄一层，贴在玻璃上，像谁用指甲刮出来的白印子。屋里很静，能听见暖气片里水流过去的声音。

牛奶的气味很淡，甜里面带一点奶腥，热的时候往上走，扑在脸上，软软的。我喝一口，烫，又放下。就这么捧着。外面灰着，冷着，赶着，我坐在这里，忽然觉得自己好像还是十几岁，放学回来，书包往地上一扔，我妈在厨房里说“先洗手”。

Bruised Lychee, Bleeding Passionfruit

Ricochets — Tropical Fruit, Sun-Drenched Green
Add to Bag Try It First — 2 ml Sample
Narrative Story

Every girl remembers her first kiss in ridiculous detail, because the first time it happens, your brain stamps it down hard, and mine is all still there. It was summer, and the air was so humid it sat on my skin like a second shirt, and she was holding a glass of something impossibly bright — passionfruit and lychee, condensation running down her wrist in little rivers — and when she laughed, the ice clinked against the glass, and I thought: I will remember this forever. I tore lychees open with my hands, not cut, torn, and the syrup ran down my wrists while she split a passionfruit and the sharp acid hit straight through the sweetness like electricity. Then we kissed, and the taste was a shock of sweet and tart, and underneath it, her skin, warm and electric and entirely new, and my heart was going so fast I was sure she could hear it. I didn't know then what I know now: that a first kiss is a sniff-test, a primal, ancient way of tasting whether someone is a match. All I knew was that the whole world seemed to swirl and melt away, like a Disney kiss, like the only two people left on earth were me and her and our lips. We laughed after, because first kisses are always a little clumsy, and that laugh is half the memory. The memory is bruised now — lychee and passionfruit, sweet but aching, the way a song you loved at seventeen can still make your chest tighten — and every time I smell that drink, I am nineteen again, and she is just a kiss away.

三、淤青荔枝，流血百香果

那杯东西是她点的。百香果，荔枝，加了很多冰，杯壁上全是水珠，顺着她的手腕往下淌。她喝东西的时候咬着吸管，眼睛看别处。我那时候十九，看她做什么都觉得好看，但嘴上不说。

后来我们接吻了。我记得的其实不是什么浪漫的味道。嘴里是冰的，她刚喝完那杯东西，舌尖上有一点甜，有一点酸，混在一起，说不清是百香果还是她自己的味道。我紧张得忘了闭眼，鼻尖碰到她的鼻尖，凉的。就那一下，脑子是空的。

现在偶尔在菜单上看到百香果荔枝，我会点一杯。喝第一口的时候，冰的还是冰的，甜的也还是甜的，但人已经不在了。那种感觉不是疼，是酸，从牙根后面慢慢泛上来，咽不下去，也吐不出来。

Crushed Coconut, Salt-Stained Rum

Quid pro quo — Solar Gourmand, Marine Amber
Add to Bag Try It First — 2 ml Sample
Narrative Story

You know the deal you make with summer, even if you never say it out loud: you hand over your plans, your schedule, your shoes, and summer hands you back your senses. The Hawaiian sun bled into the Pacific in riots of orange and violet, and I sat in the sand with a piña colada sweating in my hand, coconut cream thick on my tongue and rum warm underneath it, and the waves keeping their slow, hypnotic time against the shore. The air was thick with crushed pineapple and coconut and salt spray, and the salt was drying on my skin until it stung a little in the best way, and I wasn't sure if the dizziness in my chest was the rum or the sunset or the simple, stupid joy of being alive on a beach with nowhere else to be. Now, whenever I catch that pineapple-and-coconut sweetness on a breeze — on a city street, in a candle, in the foam of a cocktail — I am back on that sand. The scent is sun-baked and salt-stained, a reminder that some moments are so perfect they feel like a dream you get to keep. I close my eyes, and the waves are still there. I can hear them.

四、碎椰，盐渍朗姆

夏威夷那天傍晚，我在沙滩上坐了很久。太阳落下去的速度比想象中慢，海面先是金的，再是橘的，最后变成一种很深的紫，像有人把颜色一层一层往里收。杯子里的冰全化了，朗姆的味道淡得只剩一点尾巴，杯底沉着几片碎椰肉。

海风是咸的，吹在脸上黏黏的，头发贴在脖子上。浪一下一下地打，不凶，像有人在很远的地方翻书。我喝掉最后一口，甜和咸混在一起，椰子味很重，重得有点像防晒霜，但我不讨厌。

后来我回到城里，有一次在便利店闻到菠萝椰子味的润唇膏，站在货架前面愣了几秒。不是想念那片海，是想念那种感觉：坐在那里，什么都不用做，天自己会黑，浪自己会来，我什么都不用赶。

Squeezed Limoncello, Sun-Baked Stone

Ceteris paribus — Crisp Citrus, Dry Woody
Add to Bag Try It First — 2 ml Sample
Narrative Story

Some summers you don't remember as a season at all, you remember as a single afternoon that never quite ended. Tuscany in July: the lemon garden was a green cathedral, the air so thick with citrus it felt like you could drink it, and someone handed me the best lemon sorbet I have ever tasted, so cold and tart it made my eyes close on its own. It melted faster than I could eat it and spilled down the front of my white sundress in a sticky yellow streak, and I didn't even mind, because the stones under my feet were baking hot from the morning and the heat of the stone wall against my back was dry and mineral and warm. The whole afternoon felt like a secret I was keeping from the rest of the world. Now, when I wear that dress, I don't just remember the trip. I feel the sun on my shoulders and taste the lemon, and for a second I am there again: barefoot on warm stone, the scent of squeezed limoncello hanging in the air, the ghost of a summer that still lives in the fabric. All other things being equal, that one clean taste tells the whole truth.

五、挤出的柠檬酒，晒透的石头

托斯卡纳的那个柠檬园，我到现在还记得脚底下的感觉。石头被太阳晒了一整天，踩上去是温的，不烫，像一块还没凉透的面包。我穿一条白棉布裙子，裙摆蹭在小腿肚上，风一吹就鼓起来。

柠檬挂在树上，有些熟透了，黄得很凶，凑近闻，酸味冲鼻子，冲得人想打喷嚏。我在园子边上的小铺买了一小杯柠檬冰糕，木勺子挖下去，冰碴子沙沙响。第一口酸得眯眼，第二口才开始甜。

后来我每次穿那条裙子，低头闻到布料上残留的洗衣液味道，都会有一瞬间以为自己在那个园子里。不是记得，是身体先想起来了：脚底是温的，风是干的，嘴里还有一点没化完的酸。

Sunday Pillow

Tabula rasa — Fresh Floral, Soft Powdery
Add to Bag Try It First — 2 ml Sample
Narrative Story

I wake at ten, and for one terrible, electric second I think: I'm late. Then the soft, cottony truth settles over me like a second duvet. Sunday. The panic drains out of my shoulders, and I bury my face in the pillow, which smells of rose and clean linen and the warm, sun-kissed ghost of my own skin. The white duvet is a cloud; the light through the curtains is a soft, forgiving gold. I don't have to be on. I don't have to straighten my posture or sharpen my voice or be the woman whose heels make everyone in the office sit up. Nothing has been written on the day yet — no messages, no plans, no noise — and for once that doesn't frighten me at all. The rose scent is powdery and gentle, a lullaby for the senses, and I lie there and let the morning belong entirely to me. This is the luxury no one sees: a pillow that smells of nothing but rest, and a whole day that is still possible.

六、星期日的枕头

十点醒的。睁眼那一秒，心里猛地一沉——迟到了？然后看见窗帘缝里透进来的光，白得发懒，不是工作日早上那种催人的白。星期日。我把脸重新埋进枕头里。

枕套是上周换的，玫瑰味的洗衣液，味道已经不浓了，剩下一点粉粉的尾巴，混着头发上的油气和我自己的体温。被子是白的，皱成一团，我蜷在里头，脚趾碰到床单凉的那一面，缩回来，又伸过去。

不用起来。不用说话。不用把背挺直。我就这么躺着，听楼下有人遛狗，链子哗啦哗啦响，听隔壁厨房在煎东西，油锅滋啦一声。这些声音都跟我没关系。这个上午是我偷来的，谁也别想拿走。

Newborn's Blanket

de novo — Gentle Lactonic, Powdery Musk
Add to Bag Try It First — 2 ml Sample
Narrative Story

If you've ever sung a baby to sleep, you know the smell I'm talking about before I even describe it, because it gets into you in a way nothing else does. I used to sing lullabies to my little brother in the dark — lullabies I made up, half-remembered tunes — and his hands were so small that they would clench around my finger and hold on even in deep sleep, like he was afraid I'd go away if he let go. Then I would press my nose to his blanket and just breathe. It was a scent unlike any other: powdered milk, baby laundry detergent, and something else, something biological and sweet, like the cross between a French bakery and warm sheets straight out of the dryer. Science says a baby's smell lights up the brain's reward circuits and floods it with oxytocin, wiring us to bond and protect, and I believe it, because the scent of his blanket made my chest ache with a ferocity I had no name for, a wanting to stay close and keep him safe that no thought could match. It is safety from the very beginning, before anything needed forgiving, and I still reach for it.

七、新生儿的毯子

我弟小时候，手小得可怜。攥我的手指，只能攥住一根，攥得死紧，指甲掐进肉里，我疼，但不敢抽。他睡觉的时候我给他哼歌，自己瞎编的调，哼着哼着自己也困了。

他的小毯子，我闻过很多次。说不清是什么味，奶粉的甜里带一点腥，洗衣液是婴儿专用的，没什么香精，干干净净的，底下还有一点温热的、毛茸茸的气息，像小动物的肚皮。我那时候不懂什么催产素，只知道把脸埋在那条毯子里，胸口会发紧，紧得想哭。

他现在比我高了。那条毯子不知道还在不在。但有时候在超市闻到婴儿洗衣液的味道，我会站住，手心里好像又攥着那一根小手指，紧的，热的，怕我走。

His T-Shirt

Ipso facto — Warm Amber, Woody Musk
Add to Bag Try It First — 2 ml Sample
Narrative Story

Everyone has loved someone through the things they left behind, and for me it was a t-shirt, oversized and worn thin at the collar, that he left on the bed. He was a rare creature — an athletic nerd who could shred on a bass and hold his own on a drum kit, quiet unless he had something to say — but I loved him completely. I would fall asleep on his leg, my head on his thigh, and the scent of his t-shirt — clean sweat, cotton, and something warm and woody and entirely him — would be the last thing I knew before sleep. When I cried, he would pull me under his arm, and the smell of that shirt was a fortress: comfort and security and reassurance, a promise without words. It smelled like being safe. It smelled like being chosen. He is gone, and the shirt proves he was there. I still have one, you know. It's washed a thousand times now, but if I close my eyes and press my face to the cotton, I can almost find him in it.

八、他的T恤

他的衣服从来不叠，扔在椅背上，穿的时候拿起来抖一抖。我趴在他腿上睡觉，脸贴着他的大腿，闻到的就是那件T恤：棉的，洗过很多次，软了，上面有他身上的味道，不是香水，是洗衣粉、一点汗、还有皮肤本身那种温温的、带点咸的气味。

我哭的时候他不说话，胳膊一收，把我整个人圈进去。T恤的布贴在我脸上，有点粗糙，但我把鼻子埋进去，闻着那个味道，就觉得什么事都能过去。他说“没事”，声音从胸口传过来，闷闷的，震着我的耳朵。

后来分开了。那件T恤我带走了。洗过很多次，早就没有他的味道了，但我有时候还是会把脸埋进去，不是闻，是找。找那个被圈住的、什么都不用怕的感觉。

Macerated Grapes, Bleached Cork

De facto — Aromatic Wine, Earthy Woody
Add to Bag Try It First — 2 ml Sample
Narrative Story

You know how you can love a place for years before you figure out what you actually love about it? As a child, I dreaded the steakhouse. The smell hit me before the door even opened — a thick, fermented cloud of wine, wood, and something sharp, something that made my stomach turn. I thought I hated steak. Only when I grew up and started paying attention did I realize what I was actually sensitive to, and it was never the meat at all. It was the wine, dark and tannic on my tongue, sour and sweet at the same time, and the wood of the barrels, and the cork itself, rough in my fingers and stained red from years of holding the wine in. It is a scent of old money and quiet power, of dark wood and macerated grapes, and for years it made me feel like an intruder in a world I didn't belong to. Now I understand it. Now I can sit in that room and breathe it in — the fermentation, the wood, the cork — and feel not like a child who doesn't fit, but like someone who has learned the language. The label says steakhouse, but the truth is the cellar underneath, and once you name the real thing you can never un-taste it.

十、浸软的葡萄，漂白的软木

小时候跟大人去西餐厅，门一推开，那股味道就压过来。我说不清，只觉得闷，喘不上气。大人说“牛排多香”，我不说话，整顿饭都拿餐巾捂着鼻子。

长大以后才慢慢弄明白，我受不了的不是肉。是酒。是那种开了瓶的、放了一会儿的红酒，酸里带一点铁锈味，还有泡过酒的软木塞，湿的，软的，指甲一掐一个印子。再加上餐厅里那些深色木头家具，被暖气烘着，所有的味道搅在一起，变成一团很重的、化不开的东西。

现在偶尔去那样的地方吃饭，我还是会先闻到那一团东西。但我不躲了。我知道那只是酒、木头和软木，不是什么会把人吞掉的怪物。

Festive Hearth & Roasted Chestnut

Modus operandi — Warm Spicy, Heavy Gourmand
Add to Bag Try It First — 2 ml Sample
Narrative Story

Every family has a way of doing Christmas that would look like chaos to anyone else and feels like home to them, and ours is exactly that kind of chaos. It is Christmas, and the air is thick with the scent of roasting chestnuts and the sweet, smoky breath of the hearth, and we are doing what we always do: making hot cocoa, the steam fogging up the kitchen windows, and playing Carcassonne with the tiles clicking all over the table, or watching a movie together with everyone talking over the dialogue, or attempting a recipe that we will inevitably improvise. You could do these things in July, in principle, but it is not the same, because the fireplace is going and the chestnuts are roasting until the whole room smells like smoke and sugar, sweet in the heat, and the orange peel and clove hang in the air over everyone's voices. The fire pops. Someone laughs. The cocoa is too hot, and we drink it anyway. It is the smell of togetherness, of a season that asks nothing of you but to be present, to sit in the glow, to let the year end in warmth — because the chaos is the method, and the method is how we know we belong to each other.

十一、节日炉火与烤栗子

圣诞前后，家里会烤栗子。栗子用刀划一道口，丢进烤箱，过一会儿就能听见“噗”的一声，壳裂开了。整个屋子都是那种焦焦的、粉粉的甜味，混着壁炉里木头的烟。

我们在茶几上铺开卡卡颂，棋子摆得乱七八糟。热可可煮在锅里，牛奶冒泡的时候要赶紧搅，不然糊底。窗外天黑得早，四点多就暗了，但屋里灯亮着，火也亮着，谁也没急着走。

这些东西夏天也能做。但夏天做不是这个味道。夏天的热可可是多余的，炉火是荒唐的，栗子烤出来放在桌上没人想吃。十二月不一样。十二月把人都赶回屋里，赶在一起，外头越冷，里头越不想散。

Dark Slate, Rain-Struck Glass

Non sequitur — Ozonic, Mineral Woody
Add to Bag Try It First — 2 ml Sample
Narrative Story

Some people feel safest when the weather is at its worst, and if you're one of them, you already understand this scent without me explaining it. The rain begins at night, a steady drumming on the roof and against the glass that makes the world outside sound like it is being washed clean, and that sound is the whole reason my mind gets excited instead of gloomy, because rain heard from somewhere dry is safety made audible. I am in bed, the duvet pulled to my chin, a cup of coffee on the nightstand and a book in my hands, or curled up in my favorite chair in front of the fireplace, and I have never felt more safe. I still remember gathering in shelters while it rained, getting warmth from each other without minding personal space, and that feeling never left me. The window pane makes it stronger, because watching heavy rain from a warm, dry room shows you exactly where the harsh world ends and your protected space begins. There is no pressure to be productive, no obligation to be social — the weather is bad, and so the world has given me permission to do nothing but read, to be warm, to be protected. The worse the storm, the deeper the peace. The rain is a boundary, and on this side of it, I am perfectly, completely safe. By all logic the rain should make me sad. It makes me calm instead. It doesn't follow. The rain on the pane, the world can wait — I am not going anywhere.

十二、深色石板，雨打的玻璃

雨是躺下以后才开始下的。先打在窗台上，嗒，嗒，不紧不慢，像有人在外面用手指敲玻璃，试试里面有没有人。然后密起来，连成一片，哗——整面窗都湿了，路灯的光透进来，被水扯成一道道歪歪扭扭的黄。

我在被子里，肩膀露在外面有点凉，缩回去，脚碰到热水袋，还温着。雨声很大，但隔着一层玻璃，听起来闷闷的，不凶，反而让人想把被子拉高一点，把下巴埋进去。

外面越响，里面越静。没有电话，没有消息，没有“你在吗”。雨把世界关在外面了，我有了一整个晚上的许可：什么都不做。翻一页书，听一阵雨，困了就关灯。雨还在下。我哪儿也不去。

Embers & Ashen Cedar

Q.E.D. — Charred Resins, Ashen Cedar
Add to Bag Try It First — 2 ml Sample
Narrative Story

There is a particular loneliness that only comes after you've gotten everything you said you wanted, and if you've ever felt it, you know it doesn't look like sadness from the outside. It looks like a successful deal, whiskey burning slow on the tongue, a cigar between my fingers, my favorite show playing low in a room that has everything in it, and the quiet thought that I have enough money for me and still keep accumulating, for legacy, for the name after the name. In the quiet, I think of old friends, of beach bonfires, of the raw, unmistakable smell of cold woodsmoke clinging to my favorite heavy jacket like first kisses, charred logs glowing dim orange in the dark, and the cozy, grounding residue of a fire I built from scratch with my own hands. No one understands the loneliness at the top, but I share it with my cigar, and as the smoke fades my weakness fades with it. The embers and ashen cedar are a monument to a fire that once burned for other people. Some nights, I would trade every acre for that jacket.

九、余烬与灰雪松

单子签完，对方走了。我坐回车里，没急着开。西装外套搭在副驾驶，袖口沾了一点灰，是壁炉里的。刚才那间办公室里烧着木柴，火烧得不旺，烟比火多，冷木烟的味道钻进羊毛里，一时半会儿散不掉。

我打开车窗，外面是冬天傍晚的街道，车灯连成一条河。我把领带松了松，从手套箱里摸出一支雪茄，没点，就咬着。烟叶的味道干干的，带一点甜，带一点苦。

我想起以前在海边，一群人围着篝火，火快灭的时候，木头塌下去，火星子往上飘，谁往火里扔了一片湿叶子，烟“轰”地起来，呛得大家一边骂一边笑。那时候我没钱，但好像什么都不缺。现在什么都有了，车里只有我一个人，和一根没点的雪茄。
